tools.name: pdf_compress
tools.title: Compress PDF
tools.description: Shrink a PDF by re-rendering every page as a JPEG image (best for scans and photo-heavy files). Presets like the website: email (96 DPI, quality 55), balanced (144 DPI, 72), high (220 DPI, 85); or set dpi/quality yourself; optional grayscale. The result loses selectable text, links and form fields. Reports before/after size and a verdict ("bigger" means keep the original: the PDF was already efficient). Web version: https://s3eidat.github.io/pdf-compress/

tools.description: Estimate how strong a password really is, the way attackers guess (zxcvbn-style): finds common passwords (1,282-entry list), dictionary words (also reversed, capitalised or l33t), keyboard walks, sequences, repeats, years and dates, then the cheapest way to guess the whole thing. Returns a 0–4 score, entropy bits, guesses, crack time for 4 attack scenarios, the pieces found, and advice. Offline only: no breach lookups, nothing stored or logged. Web version: https://s3eidat.github.io/password-check/

password.description: The password to check (only the first 256 characters are analysed in detail).

showPieces.description: Include the matched pieces (they contain parts of the password).

bits.description: log2 of the estimated number of guesses.

output.label: Weak

crackTimes.attack: Offline, fast hash (10B / second, GPU, MD5)

tips: It contains a very common password. Attackers try those, and variations of them, first.
Capitalizing only the first letter barely helps.
Years and dates are easy to guess, especially birthdays and anniversaries.
Ending with ! or 1 is the most common trick, so attackers expect it.
Use at least 12–16 characters. Length beats complexity.
Try a passphrase of 5–6 random words (a generator picks better than people do).
Use a different password for every site. A password manager makes that painless.

output.label: Very strong

crackTimes.attack: Offline, fast hash (10B / second, GPU, MD5)

tips: Repeats like aaa or abcabc add very little over the part being repeated.
Excellent. Keep it unique to one account so a leak elsewhere can't unlock it.
Use a different password for every site. A password manager makes that painless.

tools.description: Split text, markdown or a text file into token-sized chunks for retrieval (RAG) and embeddings. tools.name: ai_ocr
tools.title: OCR (image or scanned PDF to text)
tools.description: Read the text in an image (PNG, JPEG, WebP, TIFF incl. multi-page, GIF, AVIF) or a scanned PDF with Tesseract (tesseract.js), fully offline: the English and Arabic models ship with the server and nothing is downloaded or uploaded. Languages: "eng", "ara" or "eng+ara" (default). PDF pages are rendered at 200 dpi by default. Returns the text per page and the mean word confidence (0-100); give "output" to also write a .txt file. Limits: up to 200 pages per call, roughly 1-5 s per page; printed text works well, handwriting and very small or skewed text poorly. For PDFs that already have a text layer, pdf_to_text is faster and exact. Give "file" as a local path or base64.

file.description: The image or PDF: a local file path (absolute, or relative to the server's --root) or base64 data (raw or a data: URI).

pages.description: PDF pages / TIFF frames, e.g. "1-3, 5" (default all).

dpi.description: Render resolution for PDF pages. Default 200.

psm.description: Page layout: "auto" (default), "block" (one uniform block), "line", "word", or "sparse" (scattered text).

perPage.description: Also return the text of each page separately in "pages". Default false (the joined "text" has page separators).

output.description: Also write the text to this .txt file (or folder ending in "/").

maxChars.description: Cut the inline text after this many characters (the file is never cut).

meanConfidence.description: Mean of the page confidences (0-100), pages with no text excluded.

tools.name: ai_pdf_to_markdown
tools.title: PDF to Markdown
tools.description: Convert a text PDF to structured Markdown: headings guessed from font size (text clearly larger than the body becomes #, ##, ###), paragraphs rebuilt from line spacing with hyphenated words mended, bullet and numbered lists kept, right-to-left lines in reading order. Optional page range ("1-5, 8") and page markers. Scanned PDFs without a text layer give empty pages (listed in pagesWithoutText; run OCR first). Tables and columns are read line by line. Accepts a local path or base64. Inline Markdown is cut at maxChars (default 200k); "output" saves it to a file.

file.description: The PDF: a local file path (absolute, or relative to the server's --root) or base64 data (raw or a data: URI).

pages.description: Pages to convert, e.g. "1-3, 7" or "5-" (1-based). Default: all.

password.description: Password, if the PDF is protected.

pageMarkers.description: Put "<!-- Page N -->" before each page and "---" between pages. Default false.

maxChars.description: Cut the inline Markdown after this many characters, with a note (a file written with "output" is never cut). Default 200000.

output.description: Write the Markdown to this file (or folder ending in "/") and return its path instead of the inline text.

pagesWithoutText.description: 1-based pages with no text layer (probably scanned).

bodyFontSize.description: Font size (pt) taken as body text.

truncated.description: True when the inline Markdown was cut at maxChars.

characters.description: Length of the full Markdown in characters.

words.description: Words in the text (link URLs not counted).

path.description: Written file, when "output" was given.

tools.name: ai_pptx_to_markdown
tools.title: PowerPoint (.pptx) to Markdown
tools.description: Extract the text of a PowerPoint .pptx deck as Markdown: one "## Slide N: title" section per slide in presentation order, text boxes as paragraphs and bullet lists (with indent levels), tables as Markdown tables, and speaker notes as a quote under each slide. Images, charts and SmartArt text are not extracted. Old binary .ppt is not supported. Optional "slides" range (e.g. "1-5, 8"). Accepts a local path or base64. Inline Markdown is cut at maxChars (default 200k); "output" saves it to a file. Runs locally; nothing is uploaded.

slides.description: Slides to include, e.g. "1-3, 7" or "5-" (1-based). Default: all.

maxChars.description: Cut the inline Markdown after this many characters, with a note (a file written with "output" is never cut). Default 200000.

output.description: Write the Markdown to this file (or folder ending in "/") and return its path instead of the inline text.

truncated.description: True when the inline Markdown was cut at maxChars.

characters.description: Length of the full Markdown in characters.

words.description: Words in the text (link URLs not counted).

tools.name: ai_sql_query
tools.title: SQL query over tables
tools.description: Run one read-only SQL SELECT (alasql dialect: JOIN, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY, LIMIT, UNION, WITH, subqueries, CASE, SUM/COUNT/AVG/MIN/MAX/MEDIAN/STDEV, string and date functions) over one or more tables. Each table is { name, file | csv | json }: a local path or base64 of a CSV, TSV, JSON array, JSONL or .xlsx (first sheet, or "sheet"), or inline CSV text / JSON rows. CSV cells are typed (numbers, true/false, empty → null; ISO dates stay ISO text, so they sort and compare correctly; YEAR()/MONTH() work on them). Only SELECT is allowed: INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DROP/CREATE/ALTER/ATTACH, SELECT INTO, file readers like FROM CSV(...), inline JavaScript and the -> operator are refused. Table names are case-sensitive; quote odd column names and reserved words (total, value, count, date…) as [My Column]. Returns columns and up to maxRows rows (default 500) with the total count; set "output" (.csv, .tsv, .json, .jsonl or .xlsx) to save every row to a file. Runs locally; nothing is uploaded.

query.description: One SELECT statement, e.g. SELECT region, SUM(amount) AS revenue FROM sales GROUP BY region ORDER BY revenue DESC

name.description: Table name used in the query.

file.description: A table file: local path (absolute, or relative to --root) or base64. CSV, TSV, JSON array, JSONL or .xlsx.

csv.description: Or: CSV/TSV text inline (delimiter detected; first row is the header).

json.description: Or: JSON inline: an array of objects (or of arrays, first one the header), as a value or as JSON/JSONL text.

sheet.description: For .xlsx: the sheet name to read (default: the first sheet).

format.description: Force the file format (default "auto": by extension, then by content).

tables.description: The tables the query can read (1-20).

types.description: Type CSV cells (numbers, booleans, null). Default true; false keeps every CSV cell as text.

maxRows.description: Rows to return inline (default 500). "total" always counts all rows.

output.description: Optional: save ALL result rows to this file; the type comes from the extension (.csv, .tsv, .json, .jsonl, .xlsx; default .csv).

total.description: Number of rows the query produced.

truncated.description: True when only the first maxRows rows are returned inline.

input.query: SELECT region, SUM(amount) AS revenue FROM sales GROUP BY region ORDER BY revenue DESC

tools.name: ai_text_similarity
tools.title: Text similarity and near-duplicates
tools.description: Compare two or more texts (or text files) for overlap. For every pair returns: Jaccard similarity of word shingles (k=3 words by default), a MinHash estimate of that Jaccard (128 hashes), and cosine similarity of word frequencies. Words are lower-cased, punctuation and Arabic diacritics ignored. Measures wording overlap, not meaning (no embeddings): paraphrases score low. Mode "pairs" (default) lists pairs sorted by the chosen metric; mode "dedupe" groups near-duplicates whose metric is at least "threshold" (default 0.8; groups are connected, so A~B and B~C put A, B, C together). Give "texts" (inline strings) and/or "paths" (file paths or base64). Up to 1000 texts.

paths.description: Or/also: UTF-8 text files (local paths or base64).

labels.description: Optional names for the texts, in order (texts first, then paths). Default: "#1", "#2"… or the file name.

mode.description: "pairs" (similarity of each pair) or "dedupe" (groups of near-duplicates).

metric.description: Metric used to sort pairs and to group duplicates. Default jaccard.

threshold.description: Dedupe: pairs at or above this are duplicates. Default 0.8.

maxPairs.description: Most pairs to return (highest first). Default 200.

groups.description: Dedupe: groups of 2+ near-duplicates; "keep" is the first member.

uniqueCount.description: Dedupe: texts left after keeping one per group.

tools.name: ai_token_count
tools.title: Count tokens
tools.description: Count LLM tokens in a text or text file with the OpenAI tiktoken tokenizers ("o200k_base", default, used by GPT-4o and the o-series; or "cl100k_base", used by GPT-4/3.5 and text-embedding-3). Also returns characters and words, and whether the text fits in common context windows (8k, 32k, 128k, 200k, 1M: e.g. "fits in 200k: yes"). Claude's tokenizer is not public, so for Claude the count is an estimate (typically within ~10-20%; Claude usually needs a little more), returned as a rough range. Runs locally, no API calls. Give "text" or "path" (file path or base64). Large texts (many MB) take a few seconds.

path.description: Or: a UTF-8 text/markdown file, as a local path or base64 (raw or a data: URI).

encoding.description: Tokenizer: "o200k_base" (GPT-4o / o-series, default) or "cl100k_base" (GPT-4 / GPT-3.5 / text-embedding-3).

tokens.description: Exact token count for the chosen tiktoken encoding.

characters.description: Characters (grapheme clusters, so an emoji counts once).

tools.name: ai_web_fetch
tools.title: Fetch a web page as Markdown
tools.description: Fetch a web page (http/https) and return its readable content as clean Markdown, with title, byline, final URL after redirects and a word count. Uses Mozilla Readability to keep the main article (falls back to the whole page), or a CSS "selector" you give. Respects robots.txt (refuses pages disallowed for the s3eidat-tools-mcp user agent), only reads HTML and text responses, stops at 5 MB and 20 seconds, follows up to 5 redirects, and refuses private, local and loopback addresses unless allowPrivate is true. Does not run JavaScript, so pages that build their content in the browser may come back nearly empty. Inline Markdown is cut at maxChars (default 200k); "output" saves it to a file.

url.description: The page to fetch (http:// or https://).

selector.description: CSS selector: convert only the matching elements instead of the Readability main content.

readable.description: Keep only the main content (default true). False converts the whole page body.

includeLinks.description: Keep links (made absolute) and images. False turns links into plain text and drops images.

allowPrivate.description: Allow private, local and loopback hosts (e.g. a dev server on localhost). Default false.

maxChars.description: Cut the inline Markdown after this many characters, with a note (a file written with "output" is never cut). Default 200000.

output.description: Write the Markdown to this file (or folder ending in "/") and return its path instead of the inline text.

bodyTruncated.description: True when the page was over 5 MB and only the first 5 MB were read.

truncated.description: True when the inline Markdown was cut at maxChars.

characters.description: Length of the full Markdown in characters.

words.description: Words in the text (link URLs not counted).

path.description: Written file, when "output" was given.

tools.name: ai_xlsx_to_markdown
tools.title: Excel (.xlsx/.csv) to Markdown tables
tools.description: Turn an Excel .xlsx workbook (or a .csv/.tsv file) into Markdown tables, one "## sheet" section per sheet, or only the sheet you name. The first used row is the table header; empty rows and columns around the data are dropped. Formulas show their cached result (as last saved by Excel), dates are ISO (2026-10-30, or 2026-10-30T14:05:00), merged cells show their value once, hyperlinks become Markdown links. Each sheet shows at most maxRows data rows (default 200) and says how many were left out. Old binary .xls is not supported. Accepts a local path or base64. Runs locally.

file.description: The .xlsx or .csv file: a local file path (absolute, or relative to the server's --root) or base64 data (raw or a data: URI).

sheet.description: Only this sheet: its name, or its 1-based position (e.g. "2"). Default: every sheet.

maxRows.description: Data rows to show per sheet (after the header). Default 200.

format.description: Input format. "auto" tells .xlsx (a ZIP) from CSV by its bytes.

maxChars.description: Cut the inline Markdown after this many characters, with a note (a file written with "output" is never cut). Default 200000.

output.description: Write the Markdown to this file (or folder ending in "/") and return its path instead of the inline text.

sheetNames.description: Every sheet in the workbook, in order.

truncated.description: True when the inline Markdown was cut at maxChars.

characters.description: Length of the full Markdown in characters.

words.description: Words in the text (link URLs not counted).

path.description: Written file, when "output" was given.

tools.name: ai_zip
tools.title: ZIP create / extract / list
tools.description: Work with ZIP archives locally. action "create": zip files and folders (given as paths; folders keep their own name as the top folder, symlinks are skipped) into one .zip. action "extract": unpack a .zip (path or base64) into the "output" folder; entries with "..", absolute paths or drive letters are refused (zip-slip protection), existing files are kept unless overwrite is true. action "list": entry names with sizes, no extraction. Limits: total uncompressed size 500 MB and 10000 files by default (maxTotalMB / maxFiles). Encrypted ZIPs are not supported.

files.description: create: files and folders to add (local paths).

zip.description: extract / list: the ZIP archive, a local path or base64.

output.description: create: the .zip path (or a folder ending in "/"). extract: the folder to extract into. Default: the server output folder.

overwrite.description: extract: replace files that already exist in the output folder. Default false (they are skipped).

maxTotalMB.description: Cap on the total uncompressed size, MB. Default 500.

maxFiles.description: Cap on the number of entries. Default 10000.

path.description: create: the written .zip. extract: the output folder.

bytes.description: create: size of the .zip.

files.description: Number of file entries (created, extracted, or listed).

totalSize.description: Total uncompressed size of the files, bytes.

truncated.description: list: true when only the first 5000 entries are shown.
